subjective: Inji, a male Poodle puppy approximately 70 days old, was adopted recently. The owner reports feeding him breeder-provided dry food soaked in water three times daily, with portions of about 15 grams. The puppy sometimes does not finish his food, and the owner removes the bowl and offers the same food after one to two hours. The owner notes that Inji drinks water now, although he did not previously, and is adapting to drinking water separately from food. The puppy has not been taken outside or walked on the road but is allowed on the balcony under supervision. The owner brushes him daily and cleans his eyes and ears. The puppy does not cry at night and sleeps well. The owner has not started vaccinations due to lack of vaccination documents from the breeder. The owner has been advised by the breeder on a deworming schedule and has started some home foods despite breeder advice to wait until three months of age.
objective: No physical examination findings or vital signs were documented during the consultation. The owner reports no abnormal clinical signs such as vomiting or persistent diarrhea. The puppy is eating and drinking adequately. No vaccination records are available. The puppy is currently indoors with supervised access to the balcony and no outdoor walks.
assessment: Inji is a young puppy with no current clinical illness reported. Feeding and hydration appear adequate though the puppy sometimes does not finish meals. Vaccination status is unknown due to lack of documentation. Deworming schedule is pending as per breeder's instructions. The puppy is not yet exposed to outdoor environments except supervised balcony access. No signs of illness such as persistent diarrhea or behavioral issues were noted.
plan: 1. Vaccination: Begin core puppy vaccinations (combined G, P, T, I) at three months of age, including rabies vaccination. Booster doses to follow as per standard schedule. Vaccination should not start without proper documentation. 2. Deworming: Follow breeder's deworming schedule, typically every 15 days until three months, then monthly until six months, then quarterly lifelong. 3. Feeding: Continue current feeding regimen with gradual diet changes if needed, mixing old and new food in increasing proportions. Avoid introducing home foods until three months of age, except water and breeder-approved diet. 4. Hydration: Encourage water intake; use a water fountain or small bowl as preferred. 5. Hygiene: Continue daily brushing and cleaning of eyes and ears. Dry shampoo can be used if bathing is needed. 6. Environment: Limit outdoor exposure until fully vaccinated; supervised balcony access is acceptable. Avoid unsupervised outdoor walks. 7. Monitoring: Observe for any signs of illness such as persistent diarrhea beyond two days, vomiting, or behavioral changes and consult if these occur. 8. Owner Education: Advise owner on vaccination importance, deworming schedule, gradual diet transition, and avoiding premature introduction of home foods. 9. Follow-up: Schedule vaccination appointments starting at three months of age and monitor health status regularly.
conclusion: Inji is a young Poodle puppy approximately 70 days old with adequate feeding and hydration reported by the owner. The puppy has not yet started vaccinations due to lack of documentation and has limited outdoor exposure. Deworming is planned as per breeder's schedule. The owner is advised to begin core vaccinations at three months, maintain proper hygiene, and monitor for any clinical signs. Feeding should continue with gradual diet transitions and no home foods until three months. Environmental exposure should be limited until vaccination completion. Regular follow-up and monitoring are recommended.
key_issues: 1. Vaccination status unknown due to lack of documentation; vaccination to start at three months with core vaccines and rabies. 2. Feeding regimen adequate but puppy sometimes does not finish meals; diet changes should be gradual. 3. Deworming schedule pending; follow breeder's instructions. 4. Hydration improving; encourage water intake. 5. Limited outdoor exposure; supervised balcony access only until vaccination complete.
abnormal_findings: No abnormal findings reported during consultation.
customer_instructions: 1. Begin puppy vaccinations at three months of age with combined vaccines and rabies. 2. Follow breeder's deworming schedule strictly. 3. Feed breeder-provided diet soaked in water; if changing diet, do so gradually by mixing old and new food in increasing proportions. 4. Avoid introducing home foods until three months old, except water. 5. Encourage water intake using a fountain or small bowl. 6. Maintain daily grooming including brushing and cleaning eyes and ears; dry shampoo can be used if bathing is needed. 7. Limit outdoor exposure until fully vaccinated; supervised balcony access is acceptable. 8. Monitor for diarrhea lasting more than two days or other signs of illness and consult if they occur. 9. Avoid excessive handling; holding is acceptable. 10. Wait two days after vaccination before boarding or travel.
reminders: 1. Schedule vaccination starting at three months of age. 2. Follow deworming schedule as per breeder's instructions. 3. Monitor for any signs of illness such as persistent diarrhea beyond two days. 4. Avoid outdoor exposure until vaccination is complete. 5. Wait two days after vaccination before boarding or travel.
